correctness.rationale: Invariant generator mean-zero sign change, bounded strictly positive feature and independent samples create a positive probability fixed-generator growth event; positive multiplier gives exponential expected powers. Markov L2 contraction converts that into a true-forecast MSE lower bound. Circle G=9/2, H=-1/2, the one-third negative cosine arc, ratio >=1/3 and 0<h<18 population contraction are verified directly. Independent finite arithmetic tests supplement proof.

originality.rationale: The leading 2026 paper proves fixed-horizon error control and generator-invariant exactness; previous SDMD/EDMD convergence work treats data and dictionary limits. Neither their displayed implications nor accessible closest published-finding corpus research-record claims supplies the fixed-sample universal positive-growth event with explicit smooth-circle exponential true-forecast error lower bound. Qualitative spectral pollution is known; inaccessible specialist comparisons remain a genuine risk.
residual_risks: Schurig et al. 2026 complete paper could include a stronger fixed-sample multistep spectral instability implication; only abstract was accessible.
A broader generator-EDMD spectral-pollution theorem in incompletely indexed literature may subsume the qualitative result, though the exact circle bound was not found.
The general theorem intentionally excludes dictionaries not bounded away from zero and structure-preserving stabilized fits.

value.rationale: Long-horizon prediction is a natural Koopman use; the theorem proves that no positive step or finite sample size alone ensures stable expected predictions in a broad, mathematically motivated one-feature class. It distinguishes finite-time convergence from frozen-model infinite-horizon reliability and provides a sharp smooth-circle samplewise growth floor with explicit risk exponent and probability.
